summary: Challenge to High Court's partial confirmation of Special Judge's judgment in NIA case; issue centered on procedural compliance for taking cognizance under Sections 196-A CrPC, 1989 for conspiracy (Section 120-B RPC) and cognizance under Sections 306, 411 RPC and Section 39 UAPA; Supreme Court upheld High Court's finding that no authorization under Section 196-A CrPC, 1989 was present for Section 120-B charge; affirmed that complaint under Section 4(1)(e) CrPC, 1989 requires no prescribed form; remitted charges under Sections 306, 411 RPC and Section 39 UAPA for fresh consideration, though deemed academic as Special Judge had already taken cognizance; final determination limited to interpretation and applicability of Section 196-A CrPC, 1989 versus CrPC, 1973.
final_judgment: Appeal allowed in part; upheld High Court's finding on non-compliance with Section 196-A CrPC, 1989 for charge under Section 120-B RPC; declined to interfere with charges under Sections 306, 411 RPC and Section 39 UAPA as trial was advanced and cognizance already taken; matter concerning Section 196-A CrPC, 1989 clarified.
